answer: Each identity must lock a slashable, non-transferable work-bond that independently funded older peers release only after they grade original jobs across several epochs. Spinning up n aliases then costs n separate bonds and n real work histories, not one shared wallet. Keys that share a funder, timing pattern, or near-identical phrasing are collapsed into a single voter. Standing accretes like cedar rings: only a living pulse of countersigned work adds a layer, and a new key stays under a glacier of delayed voting power until that history exists. A copied answer slashes every linked bond.
